core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a cartesian diagram using etale locality on the source, and prove the forward implication from smooth locality on the target (proof lines 7934-7943).

For the converse, shrink the target so that it is etale over an affine space over the base, write down the resulting cube, and reduce the claim to showing that a certain open subscheme of affine space equals the whole space (proof lines 7945-7973).

Handle the reduction to relative dimension at least two, and use the symmetry of the construction under the elementary automorphisms to conclude that in each fibre the open is either everything or the complement of a finite set of closed points in positive characteristic (proof lines 7975-8011).

Exclude the second possibility using the map sending each coordinate to its difference with its p-th power: the construction is symmetric under that map, the map is etale where needed, and being finite etale of degree p to the n-th power greater than one it would have to enlarge a nonempty exceptional set into a strictly larger one, a contradiction (proof lines 8011-8039).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the cartesian case and the easy direction (proof lines 7934-7943).
Reduction to a smooth neighbourhood and to an affine space (proof lines 7945-7973).
Symmetry under elementary automorphisms and the fibrewise description (proof lines 7975-8011).
The p-th power argument excluding the exceptional case (proof lines 8011-8039).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a property of morphisms which is etale local on the source, smooth local on the target and stable under postcomposition with open immersions is local on the source-and-target for the etale square condition (statement lines 7903-7932). The proof has several genuinely different stages. It first uses etale locality on the source to reduce to the case of a cartesian diagram (proof lines 7934-7938), then one direction follows from smooth locality on the target (proof lines 7940-7943). The converse is the hard part: after replacing the target by a smooth neighbourhood one reduces to the case where the target is etale over an affine space, obtains a commutative cube, and reduces the claim to exhibiting a specific open subscheme of affine space which meets every fibre; the author explicitly remarks that the naive translation-invariance argument requires extra etale localization on the target and is annoying, and instead uses the automorphisms from the group action lemma together with the case n = 1 reduction to exclude a finite exceptional set, and finally kills the remaining characteristic p possibility with the Artin-Schreier style map sending coordinates to their difference with their p-th powers, whose etaleness is checked by differentiating (proof lines 7945-8039). The claim is H3: a multi-stage reduction with an explicit strategic choice inside it and a genuinely original final step.
